issue.title: Research Fabry-Perot cavities and Fratini et al.'s later work for tools relevant to the echo
issue.body:
**What.** Research the Fabry–Pérot literature, and the later work of Fratini et al. (PRL 113, 243601 (2014), arXiv:1410.5972), for results or methods relevant to this project (Nathan, 2026-11-08). #172 found that the large-D echo profile of arXiv:2611.07007's Eq. (16), A* Re[e^{iθ}/(1 + w e^{2iθ})], is, up to a factor, the field a Fabry–Pérot cavity transmits: e^{−iφ}/(1 − r₁r₂ e^{−2iφ}) with θ = −φ and w = −r₁r₂. Its harmonic series is the sum over round trips. Read toward these questions:
- **The linear cavity.** What is known about its line shapes and their deformations (the Airy distributions, for example Ismail et al., Opt. Express 24, 16366 (2016)): extra zeros and poles, losses, dispersion. Does any of it match the rational extensions of the echo profile (#133), or the profile's branch point near its pole (EEG_PROFILE.md §3.3)?
- **Nonlinear cavities.** Kerr or "quantum mirror" cavities, the Ikeda round-trip map, and the Lugiato–Lefever equation. The critical solution is the fixed point of a one-period map, and its single unstable mode is the map's one unstable direction. Do cavity methods give tools for that fixed point, its stability or its period-doubling structure: Floquet analysis of the round-trip map, continuation, harmonic balance?
- **Fratini et al.'s further work.** Follow their later papers, through INSPIRE or Google Scholar cited-by lists, for nonlinear transport and rectification models whose stationary states are geometric sums with a nonlinear ratio.

**Why.** If the echo is literally a cavity's round-trip sum, optics may already have the analytic tools this project needs for the profile's singularity structure (#150), the selection rule, or the stability count (MODE_COUNT.md). Or the analogy may stop at the identity. Either answer is useful.

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- Every source is read, not recalled. Each is recorded in notes/LIT_REVIEW.md's ledgers (§5 searches, §6 reads), with what it does and does not contain, and its reference verified against the publisher, arXiv or INSPIRE (notes/REF_CHECK.md).
- A verdict per question: a usable result or method (named, with its equation), an analogy only, or nothing found in the sources searched.
- For each usable item, a proposed follow-up task with a check that can fail.
- No novelty sentence is written anywhere.

**Depends on.** #172.

comments.body: started: subagent of the coordinator on the Apple M5 Mac (mac), worktree agent-ac725c1bf55baff6f, 1 thread (literature search through WebSearch and WebFetch, no computation). Raw notes go to choptuik-large-d-raw folder I198-mac/, the work in progress to wip/i198.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 01:11 UTC (mac, subagent).** Machine: CPU 50% idle, memory 30 GB used of 32 GB (other jobs); this task runs no computation beyond a 30-digit identity check.

- Searches: 24 web queries and 4 INSPIRE queries so far. Reads: 18 sources in full or in part, plus records and abstracts (Pollnau–Eichhorn 2020, Sánchez-Soto–Monzón–Leuchs 2016, Marques–Guggenheim–Munro 2021, Hansson–Wabnitz 2015, Conforti et al., Parra-Rivas et al., Gomila–Matías–Colet, Maitland et al., Fratini et al. 2014 and four of its follow-ups). Ismail et al. 2016 itself could not be opened (Optica returns a loading page), so its content comes through Pollnau–Eichhorn and Wikipedia.
- INSPIRE: Fratini et al. is recid 3025790 with 57 citing records; Fratini's own later work in this line is one paper (Fratini–Ghobadi 2016, 21 citing records).
- One identity found and checked (inferred, `I198-mac/identity_check.py`, exit 0; its mutation fails all four checks): at δ = 0, Eq. (16) is cos θ times the cavity's Airy distribution with coefficient of finesse F = 4q/(1−q)², so its hump threshold q_c = 3 − 2√2 is Pollnau–Eichhorn's Eq. (118), the reflectivity at which the Airy linewidth stops being defined.
- Raw folder `I198-mac/`, commit abc0f30 (merged as 9a9a77b). Writing the addendum next.

**Closing summary, 2026-11-09 01:23 UTC (mac, subagent).** Machine: CPU 63% idle, memory 31 GB used of 32 GB (other jobs). Nothing heavy ran; the only computation is a 30-digit identity check.

The record is the new addendum at the end of `notes/LIT_REVIEW.md` ("Addendum (2026-11-09, issue #198)"), with entries in its §5 search ledger and §6 read ledger. Branch `wip/i198`, head 20c80c1. Raw folder `I198-mac/` of the raw-data repository, commit a3abcb5. It holds the search log, the read log with quotes, the 57 citing records of Fratini et al., and `identity_check.py` with its two logs.

## Verdicts

| Question | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Q1, the linear cavity | **An analogy only.** The Airy distribution and its Lorentzian pole-pair decomposition restate what EEG_PROFILE.md §2 already has: the Poisson-kernel denominator, one pole pair per half period, and pole distance equal to decay rate. Losses only rescale \|w\|. The reflected field and multi-stage cavities give the [1/1] and [L/N] rational class of #133 (*inferred*), with no reason for any particular L, N. The one mechanism found that turns a pole into a branch point is the angular Airy function (Marques et al., Eq. (3)). It spreads the round-trip *phase*, so the cut runs along Re θ, and a Gaussian beam gives \|r_{k+1} − r_k\| ~ k⁻³. The tuned profile's Padé poles run along Im θ (a spread of *loss*) and its differences go as k⁻⁴ (EEG_PROFILE.md §8.5, conditional on Conjecture 1). No source read treats a spread of loss. |
| Q2, nonlinear cavities | **An analogy only.** The methods exist and the project already has counterparts. Floquet analysis uses the eigenvalues of the one-round-trip matrix (Hansson–Wabnitz Eq. (11); Conforti et al., \|Δ\| > 1 + W). There the matrix is 2×2 because the background is homogeneous; the echo's is not, and the counterpart is det M(λ) with its winding count. Continuation is predictor–corrector (Parra-Rivas et al.), against the project's higher-order ANM. Harmonic balance is the modal expansion versus the LLE. Averaging into the LLE needs high finesse, and the echo has F = 0.247. In cavities, period doubling is a bifurcation (the q₋ eigenvalue), whereas the echo's odd harmonics are a symmetry. The middle-branch saddle with "a single unstable direction" and its law T ∝ −(1/λ₁) ln(θ_c − θ) (Gomila et al.) is the γ = 1/λ mechanism, seen in a cavity. |
| Q3, Fratini et al.'s later work | **Nothing found in the sources searched.** Fratini et al. (2014) solves its geometric sum with a power-dependent ratio, (S.2) and (S.7), numerically, with no multiplicity or stability analysis. Its successors (Fratini–Ghobadi 2016, Mascarenhas et al. 2016, Almeida et al. 2019) and four citing abstracts use full-quantum models with no round-trip sum. The classical antecedents are the Ikeda fixed point and Felber–Marburger's Kerr Fabry–Pérot, which was not read. |

## Identities (*inferred*, checked by `I198-mac/identity_check.py`, exit 0; its mutation fails all six, exit 1)

1. At δ = 0, Eq. (16) is A*(1+q)/(1−q)² · cos θ · 𝒜(θ + π/2), the Airy distribution with coefficient of finesse F = 4q/(1−q)².
2. Therefore EEG_PROFILE.md §2's hump threshold q_c = 3 − 2√2 is F = 1. That is Pollnau–Eichhorn's Eq. (118), (3 − 2√2)² = 17 − 12√2, where the Airy FWHM stops being defined.
3. The Lorentzian half-width is Eq. (16)'s pole distance, ½ ln(1/q) = 1.4493.
4. Eq. (114), Lorentzian linewidth = free spectral range, is 2σ = π, at q = e^{−π}.
5. and 6. Smeared poles: a phase spread with a finite edge gives differences ~ k⁻³; a loss spread with a linear edge gives k⁻⁴.

| at EEG26b's q = 0.0551 | value |
|---|---|
| coefficient of finesse F | 0.247 (< 1, so the Airy linewidth is undefined) |
| Lorentzian finesse π/(2σ) | 1.084 |
| Eq. (114) threshold e^{−π} | 0.0432 |
| hump threshold 3 − 2√2 | 0.1716 |

## Closest works (what each does and does not contain)

- **Pollnau–Eichhorn, Prog. Quantum Electron. 72, 100255 (2020).** Contains the Airy distribution as an exact sum of Lorentzian pole pairs (Eqs. (99)–(108)), the linewidth thresholds (Eqs. (114), (118)), loss (Eqs. (111)–(112)), and a statement that a frequency-dependent reflectivity distorts the lines. Does not contain any form for that reflectivity, extra poles or zeros, or branch points.
- **Ismail et al., Opt. Express 24, 16366 (2016).** FULL-TEXT-UNREAD (Optica returned a loading page). Known only through Pollnau–Eichhorn and Wikipedia.
- **Sánchez-Soto–Monzón–Leuchs, Eur. J. Phys. 37, 064001 (2016).** Contains the round-trip sum, the self-consistent field, the impulse response, and the Lorentzian sum, Eq. (3.7). Does not contain losses, coupled cavities or nonlinear effects.
- **Marques–Guggenheim–Munro, Opt. Express 29, 24144 (2021).** Contains the transmission and reflection Airy functions (Eq. (1)) and the angular Airy function (Eq. (3)), with the asymmetric, broadened lines of focused beams. Does not contain the analytic structure of the averaged line.
- **Hansson–Wabnitz, JOSA B 32, 1259 (2015).** Contains the Ikeda map and its fixed point, a geometric sum with a field-dependent ratio (Eqs. (4)–(5), one or three states), Floquet eigenvalues q± (Eq. (11)) with q₋ giving period doubling, and the limits of the LLE. Does not contain continuation or harmonic balance.
- **Conforti et al., Opt. Lett. 39, 4200 (2014).** Contains a 2×2 monodromy matrix and the Floquet discriminant criterion. Does not contain continuation, harmonic balance or Hill's method.
- **Gomila–Matías–Colet, PRL 94, 063905 (2005).** Contains a saddle with a single unstable direction and the logarithmic period law (slope 5.60 measured, 5.65 predicted). Does not say how the eigenvalue was computed.
- **Parra-Rivas et al., arXiv:2010.03375.** Contains predictor–corrector continuation with Jacobian eigenvalues, and a period-doubling cascade of breathers. Does not contain continuation of the periodic orbits or Floquet multipliers.
- **Maitland et al., PRR 2, 043195 (2020).** Contains coupled loops with eigenvalue pairs ±λ. Does not contain a symmetry reduction.
- **Fratini et al., PRL 113, 243601 (2014)** and its successors: see Q3.

## Ledger summary

- **Searches:** 25 web queries and 4 INSPIRE queries (`arxiv 1410.5972`, recid 3025790 with 57 citations; `refersto:recid:3025790`, 57 records; Fratini's author records, 17; `refersto:recid:3027964`, 21).
- **Reads:** 19 sources opened, 13 in full or in part and 6 as abstracts or lists, plus records of 9 more.
- **PDFs** that came back as binary were extracted with pypdf from the tool's saved copy. That opened Pollnau–Eichhorn and Marques et al.
- **Not read:** Ismail et al., Ikeda (1979), Ikeda–Daido–Akimoto (1980), Felber–Marburger (1978), Lugiato–Lefever (1987), Coen–Haelterman (1997), Haelterman–Trillo–Wabnitz (1992), Chembo–Yu (2010) and Madsen–Zhao (records only).
- **Google Scholar's cited-by list was not reached.** 51 of the 57 INSPIRE citers rest on titles.

## Discrepancies

- None with the repository's text.
- One pointer for whoever verifies Svelto's *Principles of Lasers*, 5th ed. Wikipedia, as #172 recorded it, cites ch. 4.5.1; Pollnau–Eichhorn cite pp. 169–171, Ch. 5.3. They may refer to different passages, and neither was checked against the book.

No novelty sentence was written. Proposed text for EEG_PROFILE.md §2 (identities 1 and 2) is in the addendum's last subsection.

## Recommended tasks

1. **The direction of the echo's branch cut: a planted test with smeared poles.**
   - *What:* add a loss-spread plant and a phase-spread plant, both with a linear edge, to `solver/eeg_profile/rational_fit.py`'s planted-truth path. Run the Padé pole march of EEG_PROFILE.md §8.3 on both, then on the tuned data.
   - *Why:* this decides which class of smeared pole the profile's branch point belongs to, for #150.
   - *Acceptance:* the loss plant's second pole marches with \|ΔRe θ₂\| < 0.3 \|ΔIm θ₂\|, and the phase plant's with \|ΔIm θ₂\| < 0.3 \|ΔRe θ₂\| (n = 2 to 4). The test fails if both march the same way, and the real-data verdict is then void. The real-data direction is reported conditional on Conjecture 1.
   - *Depends on:* #133, #198. Minutes on one core.
2. **Read the cavity sources that did not open.**
   - *What:* Ismail et al. 2016, Felber–Marburger 1978, Ikeda 1979 and Coen–Haelterman 1997, through a channel that renders Optica and APS pages.
   - *Why:* the Q1 and Q2 verdicts rest on secondary accounts of these four.
   - *Acceptance:* each is read in full and logged in §6. The task reports failure if any of them contains a closed form for a frequency-dependent reflectivity, a branch point at a cavity pole, or a stability method for a non-homogeneous fixed point that the verdicts miss.
   - *Depends on:* #198.

Leaving the issue open for the coordinator.

Coordinator review. I reran `I198-mac/identity_check.py` (exit 0, all six) and its mutation (exit 1). Merged as 8a46094. The proposed text for EEG_PROFILE.md §2, that the hump threshold q_c = 3 − 2√2 is the Fabry–Pérot finesse F = 1, is in 9a39cdb, with Pollnau–Eichhorn's Eq. (118) credited. Verdicts: analogies only for questions 1 and 2, nothing found in the sources searched for question 3. The recommended tasks are #216 (the branch-cut direction) and #217 (the unread sources).
